title: Kubric: A Scalable Dataset Generator
abstract: A scalable synthetic dataset generator; retained here because TCOW's official project page says it leverages Kubric to generate accurate occlusion and containment labels, and CoTracker3's official repository documents a Kubric-rendered training set.
query: snowball:TCOW official project -> Kubric simulator; CoTracker3 official repository -> Kubric rendered training sequences
citation_path: TCOW official page explicitly states that it leverages the Kubric simulator to generate accurate labels for occlusion and containment. CoTracker3 official repository states that its released Kubric dataset contains 6,000 rendered 512x512, 120-frame sequences.

title: SAIL-VOS: Semantic Amodal Instance Level Video Object Segmentation -- A Synthetic Dataset and Baselines
abstract: Synthetic amodal video dataset from GTA-V. Its public documentation states that the dataset provides RGB, modal masks, amodal masks and persistent object identifiers across frames.
citation_path: S-AModal arXiv related-work section identifies SAIL-VOS as an amodal-video segmentation dataset/baseline; the official SAIL-VOS site documents the modal and amodal label layout.

title: PointOdyssey: A Large-Scale Synthetic Dataset for Long-Term Point Tracking
abstract: Long-video synthetic point-tracking dataset and rendering framework with RGB, depth, normals, instance segmentation, camera parameters, 2D/3D trajectories and visibility labels. The official project reports naturalistic motion, randomized assets/materials/lighting and animal subjects.
query: snowball:S-AModal related work -> PIPs++/PointOdyssey; CoTracker3 temporal-training comparator
citation_path: S-AModal's related-work section names PIPs++/PointOdyssey among point-trackers; PointOdyssey's official paper/project documents the synthetic temporal-label design.

title: Self-supervised Amodal Video Object Segmentation
abstract: SaVos uses video temporal information and visible object parts as self-supervision for amodal masks; it reports synthetic FISHBOWL and real KINS-Video-Car evaluation and releases official code.
citation_path: S-AModal directly identifies SAVOS as its closest self-supervised amodal-VIS comparator, and states that SAVOS uses image, visible mask and optical flow.

title: Foundation Models for Amodal Video Instance Segmentation in Automated Driving
abstract: S-AModal fine-tunes SAM for image-level amodal segmentation and extends it to video through visible-mask point prompts, memory, and point tracking. It explicitly separates the amodal mask predictor from a visible VIS front end rather than learning detector transfer.
query: snowball:SAMEO/TCOW/SAMBA related foundation-model video amodal work
citation_path: This is a directly relevant paper surfaced while following the SAM-based amodal-video branch from the seed set; its official code cites ECCV-VCAD 2024 and provides the stated pipeline.

title: CoTracker: It is Better to Track Together
abstract: Joint transformer point tracker for long video sequences. The official paper says it can track occluded and out-of-view points; it is causal on short windows but trained with unrolled recurrent windows.
citation_path: S-AModal directly states that it chooses CoTracker to track point prompts through an occluded instance; its released code pins a CoTracker dependency.

title: TAPIR: Tracking Any Point with per-Frame Initialization and Temporal Refinement
abstract: Point tracker with a per-frame matching stage and temporal refinement, with a documented positional-uncertainty output. Its project page evaluates point location and occlusion using TAP-Vid Average Jaccard.
citation_path: S-AModal's related-work section names TAPIR as a tracker combining TAP-Net and PIPs; this supports a point-visibility auxiliary target, not amodal-mask completion by itself.

title: TAP-Vid: A Benchmark for Tracking Any Point in a Video
abstract: Benchmark with real human-annotated and synthetic point tracks. The official documentation requires algorithms to predict both point position and visibility, making it a clean evaluation precedent for temporal occlusion outputs.
citation_path: S-AModal's related-work section cites TAP-Vid as the benchmark that formalizes tracking any point and identifying its occlusion state.

title: pix2gestalt: Amodal Segmentation by Synthesizing Wholes
abstract: Zero-shot amodal segmentation/completion with conditional diffusion trained on synthetically curated occluded-object/whole-object pairs. It is a published direct precedent for paired visibility-to-whole supervision.
query: snowball:SAMBA and Amodal SAM related work -> pix2gestalt
citation_path: SAMBA's official CVPR abstract contrasts its SAM-based design with pix2gestalt; Amodal SAM's official arXiv evaluation section also names pix2gestalt as a zero-shot comparator.

title: Towards Efficient Foundation Model for Zero-shot Amodal Segmentation
abstract: SAMBA jointly learns modal and amodal segmentation via separation-to-fusion and uses an occlusion-rate-aware mixture of experts with a distribution loss. It is a direct novelty conflict for any claim to be first to separate visible and complete branches or condition a model on occlusion rate.
citation_path: Official CVPR 2025 page/paper. Its published abstract explicitly describes joint modal/amodal learning and experts associated with distinct occlusion rates.
